title: Why Did Rome Fall?
objective: After this level you can compare the main explanations for the fall of the Western Empire.
summary: Invasions, civil wars and the loss of Africa broke the West. Gibbon blamed Christianity and lost virtue; others see a transformation.

cards.headline: Historians have given many answers to why the West fell. Here are the big ones.
cards.body: The West fell in 476 CE. Fine. But why? Historians have proposed many answers, and one twist: maybe “fall” is the wrong word.

cards.headline: Outside and inside
cards.body: Start with the squeeze. From outside, pressure from Germanic peoples and the Huns stretched the western army beyond its limits. From inside, repeated civil wars between Roman generals weakened the West further. Then came the money. When the Vandals captured Carthage in 439 CE, the West lost its richest tax base and a major grain supply. Enemies at the door, fights in the house, and an empty pantry.

cards.headline: Fall or transformation?
cards.body: The classic answer came from Edward Gibbon, the historian who called the age of the Five Good Emperors the happiest (Level 60). His The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire blamed, in part, the rise of Christianity and a loss of civic virtue. Some historians today tell it differently: not a sudden collapse, but a transformation into the kingdoms of medieval Europe. Less a house falling down, more a house slowly remodeled by new owners.

cards.context: The East was richer and more populous than the West, which helps explain why it outlived the West by nearly a thousand years (you’ll meet it next level). Two halves of one empire, and the one with more money and more people was the one still standing.

cards.headline: The fall: debated
learned: Losing Africa cost taxes and grain

questions.prompt: What did the West lose when the Vandals took Carthage in 439 CE?

options.label: Its only fleet of warships
options.rationale: The loss was money and food.

options.label: Its last Roman legion
options.rationale: The loss was money and food.

questions.explanation: Africa was the West’s richest tax base and a major grain supply.

questions.prompt: Why do some historians prefer “transformation” to “fall”?

options.label: The West was never actually invaded
The West changed gradually into new kingdoms
Rome was rebuilt better within ten years
The East peacefully absorbed the whole West

questions.explanation: They see Roman ways blending into the kingdoms of medieval Europe rather than a sudden collapse.
